items.title: How Knowledge Graphs Make AI Smarter
items.summary:
If you’ve ever wondered how to make LLMs smarter, more reliable, and less hallucination-prone, this is the perfect place to start.

In this video, we break down Chapter 1 of Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action—a clear, eye-opening introduction to the world of knowledge graphs and why they’re becoming essential in next-generation AI systems. The authors—Alessandro Negro, Vlastimil Kus, Giuseppe Futia, and Fabio Montagna—show how KGs add structure, meaning, and context to data, giving LLMs a foundation they can trust.

You’ll learn:
-What knowledge graphs really are (beyond the buzzwords)
- Why companies use them to ground their AI in real-world facts
- How KGs and LLMs complement each other—and why this combination is so powerful
- The essential mental models you need to understand knowledge-driven AI

If you’re building, evaluating, or even just curious about hybrid AI systems, this summary gives you a strong grasp of the ideas shaping the future of intelligent applications.

👉 Save 40% with code WATCHNEGRO40 at https://hubs.la/Q03TKkK90

🔥 Perfect for:
- Developers who want LLMs that reason better
- Data engineers and knowledge-graph practitioners
- ML/NLP professionals building retrieval- or graph-augmented models
- Anyone who wants to understand the real foundation of knowledge-aware AI

💬 Have thoughts or questions?
Drop them in the comments—let’s talk about how you’re connecting (or want to connect) structured knowledge and language models.

Thanks for watching—and welcome to the intersection where knowledge meets intelligence.

items.title: DR Tulu | An open, end-to-end training recipe for long-form deep research
items.summary: Deep Research Tulu (DR Tulu), the first open model that is directly trained for long-form deep research tasks through an end-to-end training recipe that combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics (RLER). DR Tulu starts from a strong base model and progresses through multiple training stages: SFT on high-quality, naturally occurring information-seeking queries, followed by online RL with RLER tailored to long-form research.
